terms: be very hot/have a high fever
definition: <sa>, hot, and <gawp> written as one word; after {a ci}, the body, it is have a high fever
the number seven; it stands after the noun it counts, and {a ni sagih ni} is the seventh day
<sagih>, seven, with the ending <in>; {a zah sagihin} is seven times as much
<sagih>, seven, with the ending <in>; {a zah sagihin kithuk} is be avenged seven times over
<sagih>, seven, with the ordinal ending <na>: the seventh in a series; {kha sagihna} is the seventh month
<sagih>, seven, with the plural marker <te>: the seven of a group already mentioned
<sagih>, seven, with the plural <te>, written with a capital: the seven men chosen in Jerusalem to serve at tables
<sagih>, seven, with <vei>, times: seven times
<sagihvei>, seven times, with <na>, making the ordinal: the seventh time
<sa>, meat or animal, with <gil>, belly: the entrails of a slaughtered animal, cleaned and cooked at a feast; {sagil bawl} is prepare them
<sa>, animal, and <go>, slaughter, written as one word: the killing of an animal, here as an offering in {sagoh biakpiakna}, animal sacrifice
<sa>, animal or meat, with <guh>, bone: a bone of a carcass, as gnawed by beasts
<saguh> with the plural <te>: the bones in a pot of meat
a muscle of the body, from <sa>, flesh, and <gui>, cord
thick, of a wall or of cloud and darkness; after a measure it says how thick a thing is, as {tong nga sah}, five cubits thick
a fierce wild animal; in Revelation, the beast that rises from the Abyss

the tiger, the large striped wild cat, as kept in a zoo and hunted in the hills; named beside <humpi>, lion, and <kamkei>, leopard, as a different animal, where the Bible rows have only the general wild beast
Saying: having a tiger for a grandfather; the book lists it among its idiomatic expressions without explaining it, apparently said of one who has a strong and feared backer
<sahang>, wild beast, with the plural <te>

<sa>, meat, and <hawm>, share out, written as one word: the customary sharing out of meat at a feast, often paired as {zuhawm sahawm}, the sharing of beer and meat; {vompi sahawm}, sharing bear meat, is said of an unequal division
<sahawm> with the noun ending {-na}: the customary sharing out of the meat of a slaughtered animal among the kin
<sahawm>, the sharing out of meat, with <zia>, way: the customary manner in which the meat of a feast is divided
tobacco that is held in the mouth or chewed, named beside cigarettes, <khaini> and <kunza> among harmful habits

terms: not think at all/not consider at all/not mind at all
definition: <sa>, here think or feel something to be so, with <hetlo>, not at all, written as one word and placed after a describing word: {dik sahetlo} is not think it right at all, {phamawh sahetlo} not mind at all
<sah>, thick, with the linking ending <in>, joining it to the next description
<sah> and <lua> written as one word: too thick, mostly of fog, cloud or smoke through which nothing can be seen
<sah>, thick, and <mahmah>, very, written as one word: very thick, said of smoke and of a layer of material
<sah>, thick, with the noun ending <na>: how thick a thing is, used in measurements of walls and vessels
<sah>, thick, with the augmentative <pi>; said of cloud, darkness and a shield
<sahpi>, thick, with the plural <te>: said of thick clouds and thick darkness
in the saying about the eye of a needle the Tedim text has {sai} where the English has camel
look after a household or task; {kumpi-inn sung a sai}, the one in charge of the palace; {kigal sai}, opposite each other, is a separate expression
in {anlum sai}, bread shop, where the English has the street of the bakers
<sai>, elephant, with the marker <in> written with a hyphen
a shop or stall where goods are sold; {vanzuakna saidawl} is a shop selling goods
a shop or stall where things are sold or a service is given; {anzuakna saigei} is a food stall
elephant tusk, from <sai>, elephant, and <ha>, tooth; a costly material for thrones and houses
part of the word <saihadial>, linen, written here as two words: {saiha dial puan} is linen cloth
linen, a fine cloth; mostly {saihadial puan}, a linen cloth or garment
<saiha>, elephant tusk, with <paak>: ivory as a traded and smuggled good; what <paak> adds here is not certain
the tusk of an elephant and the ivory from it, from <saiha>, ivory; a thing of great value
<saiha>, ivory, with the plural <te>: things made of ivory
set one person or thing against another to see which has more of a quality; the one compared with takes <tawh>; the book uses it beside <tehkak> for the comparison of adjectives
<saikak>, compare, with the noun suffix <na>: the comparing of two or more people or things
<saikakna>, comparison, with the place marker <ah>: in comparing
a two-wheeled vehicle: a bicycle, and in present-day writing mostly a motorcycle, also called {mawtaw saikel}
town in Samaria near Jacob’s well, where Jesus spoke with the Samaritan woman
<sai>, shop, and <khat> written as one word: a shop, a stall or an eating place
weapon for throwing stones; {saili kuang} is the pouch of the sling and <sailungtang> the sling stone
the stone shot from a {saili}, sling
<sai>, shop, and <mai>, front, written as one word: the front of a shop or restaurant; {saimai ah} is in front of the shop
hill about 6500 feet high at the entrance of Tedim town, with a view over the town and a place of prayer
<sa> as the marker of a completed state and <in> written as one word after a verb or describing word: in that state, while being so or doing so
<sai.2>, manage or attend to, with the noun suffix <na>: the handling or running of a matter
<sai>, shop, with <nei>, have: the owner of a shop or restaurant
<sainei>, shop owner, with <nu> for a woman: the woman who owns a shop or stall
<sainei> and <pa> written as one word: the man who owns a shop
<sai>, shop, with <ngak>, keep watch: the person who minds a shop and serves its customers
misprint for <Siangtho> in {Kha Saingtho}, the Holy Spirit
<sai>, be in charge of, with <pa>, a man: {inn sung saipa} is the man in charge of the palace or household
<sai>, elephant, with <pi>, big; the Tedim text has it where the English has camel
a large shop or eating place, from the Burmese loan <sai>, shop, with <pi>, big, and not the animal; {an saipi} is a big restaurant
the head of a government ministry, named after the matter in charge as in {gamsung vai saipi}, minister of home affairs

terms: be involved in/concern oneself with/deal with
definition: <sai>, attend to, with the ending {-pih}, together with: take a matter up and busy oneself with it; {va saipih} is step into the affair of another; with <ki> or <aki> before it, what one is engaged in
large island in the eastern Mediterranean Sea, home of Barnabas
king of Persia who took Babylon and let the Jewish exiles return to rebuild the temple
city in Libya on the north coast of Africa, home of Simon who carried the cross of Jesus
<sai>, elephant, with <sa>, meat: the meat of an elephant, used in a comparison
placed after a verb: the action is done in haste or with bustle; {kizen saisai} is busy and energetic

terms: arrange for/take care of for/handle for
definition: <sai>, attend to, with <sak>, do for someone: see to a matter on behalf of someone else
<sai>, shop, with <sung>, inside, written as one word: the inside of a shop, the shop premises; {saisung ah} is in the shop
<saisung>, the inside of a shop, and <ah> written as one word: in the shop

terms: the whole shop/all through the shop
definition: <saisung>, the inside of a shop, and <teng>, all, written as one word: the whole of the shop or of the shops
<sai>, shop, with the plural <te>: shops, stalls or businesses

<sai>, be in charge of, with the plural <te>, placed after the name of a matter: the people or offices that deal with it, as in <thuthak saite>, news agencies, and {cidamna lam saite}, the health authorities
<sai>, shop, with the plural <te> and the subject marker <in> written as one word; in news writing {thuthak saiten} is the news outlets, as the subject of saying or reporting
<sai>, shop, and <zuak>, sell, written as one word: a person who sells at a shop or stall, or the work of keeping a shop
<sai>, shop, and <zuakpa>, seller, written as one word: the man who sells in a shop
particle suffixed to form verb past tense
postpositional marker indicating future action or state, equivalent in usage to the auxiliary verbs will and shall
form of <sa>, feel or think, after a word of quality: {nuam sak} is find pleasant, {thupi sak} regard as important, {lamdang sak} find strange; not the causing {sak} that follows a verb
form of <sa>, sing, used before a noun and in dependent clauses: {a sak la} is the song that he sings
hard to the touch, not soft; the opposite of <nip>, soft
the causative <sak> with the linking <a> written as one word, placed after a verb: have something done and then go on, as in {bawl saka}, had it made and
poetic word for <sahang>, used in songs
fourth son of Obed-Edom, a gatekeeper of the temple

{la sak}, sing a song, with <dan>, manner, the two last written as one word: the way a song is sung; the same spelling also joins the causative <sak> and <dan>, the way of making something so
the causative <sak> and <den>, always, written as one word after a verb: keep causing, as in {nawngkai sakden}, keep on troubling
<sak> and <ding> written as one word after a verb: will make it happen, will do it for someone
<sak> and <dingin> written as one word after a verb: in order to make it happen or to do it for someone
<sak>, the causative placed after a verb, and <dingpen>, what is to be, written as one word: makes the clause the topic, what will cause the thing to happen, or that it should be made to happen

terms: I do not find/I do not consider
definition: <sa.5>, feel or consider, with the ending -keng, a short form of <kei> <ing>, I do not, written as one word: {thupi sakeng} is I do not consider it important

the causative <sak>, make or cause, and <gawp>, severely, written as one word after a verb: cause it badly or do it to someone with violence, as in {lauthawng sakgawp}, frighten badly, and {suksiat sakgawp}, wreck
<sa>, here think or consider a thing to be so, with <kha>: happen to think, suppose, often wrongly; {sakha kei ni} is let us not suppose
a camp or post, especially of soldiers or an armed group; {thong sakhan} is a prison camp
village in Myanmar, named as the home village of Zomi people and as a place of fighting
the Hararite, father of Ahiam, one of the mighty warriors of David
<sa>, flesh, with <khat>, one: a single body, said of husband and wife, and of parts made in one piece with something else

terms: of one piece/in one piece/as one piece
definition: <sakhat>, one piece, with the ending <in>: made in one piece with something else
a bag carried slung from the shoulder; worn with the verb <kuah>, like <namsau>, a sword, and <thungip>
<sa>, sing, with <khawm>, together: sing together, said with <la>, song
the Hararite, father of Ahiam, one of the mighty warriors of David
a small wild deer; the Bible uses it for deer and gazelles, often named together with <sanang>
Saying: of the deer the mother is red and the young is red; each one takes after his own mother and father
name of the custom by which a household that has no brother to fill a position appoints a trusted man of the same age instead; literally a deer looking for a clan
Saying: one who cannot kill a deer goes for the big boar; said of those who aim at great things without first managing the small ones
<sakhi>, deer, with the subject marker <in>: the deer, as the doer of the action

a Benjamite, son of Shaharaim and head of a family
<sa.5>, feel or consider, and <khin>, already, written as one word: {lamdang sakhin} is already find strange; the same spelling also stands for {sa khin}, have already sung
<sakhi> deer with <no>, young: the young of a deer
<sakhi> deer with <pi>, female: a female deer
<sakhipi>, doe, with the plural <te>; the feet of does are a picture of sure footing on high places
<sakhi> deer with <tal>, the male of an animal; named among the clean animals that may be eaten
<sakhital>, stag, with <no>, young: a young stag, a picture of the beloved in the Song of Solomon
<sakhital>, stag, with the plural <te>
plural of <sakhi>; the Bible uses it for deer, gazelles and does, and in Psalm 104 for the hyrax
the rainbow, set in the clouds as the sign of the covenant of God with Noah
<sa>, animal, with <ki>, horn: the horn of an animal, also a horn blown as a trumpet; in the visions of Zechariah horns stand for the powers of the nations
a small animal of the rocks, named among the unclean animals because it chews the cud but has no divided hoof
<sakikh> written with a capital at the start of a sentence
<sakikh>, hyrax, with the plural <te>
causative <sak> with the linking suffix <in>, placed after a verb: making or letting someone do it, and then going on to the next action
<saki>, a horn blown as an instrument, with the plural <te>
<sak>, cause or find to be, and <kei>, not, written as one word after a verb or describing word: not make or let it happen, not find it so; {sakkei in} forbids, do not let
the causative <sak> with <kha>, happen to, written as one word after a verb: bring something about without meaning to, or happen to do it to someone

<sak>, the form of <sa> feel or consider, with <khawm> together; {nuam sakkhawm}, be glad together with someone
the causative <sak> and <khin>, already, written as one word after a verb: has already been made to happen, has already been done to someone
<sak>, the form of <sa> sing, with <khit> finished
sing, as in {la sak}, sing a song, with <khop>, together, written as one word: sing a song together
causative <sak> with <kik>, again or back, placed after a verb: make something be or stand again, restore
the part of a song or hymn that is sung again after each verse, from <sak>, sing, with <kik>, again; mostly as {a sakkik}, its chorus
a star god named together with Kaiwan in Amos, whose image Israel made and worshipped
causative <sak> with <lai>, here still, written as one word after a verb: still let something go on, still have it done
the north, the opposite of <khanglam>, south; {saklam huih} is the north wind and {saklam gam} the land of the north
<saklam> north with <ah> in, at
<sak> and <leh>, if, written as one word after a verb: if one lets or makes it happen; after <ka>, when I think it so
the causing <sak> after a verb and <lel>, merely, written as one word: only makes it so, does nothing but cause it
the causative <sak> and <lo>, not, written as one word after a verb: not make, not let, not allow to happen
the causative <sak> with <lo> and <ding> written as one word after a verb: will not make it so, so as not to cause it

<saklo>, not make, with the plural ending <te>: those who do not make a thing happen
the causative <sak> with <lua>, too much, written as one word after a verb or describing word: make someone or something too much so, as {gilkial saklua}, let someone get too hungry
<sak>, the form of <sa> feel or consider, with <luat> too much; {haksa a sakluat}, what he found too hard
<sak> and <mahmah> written as one word: after a word of quality, find it very much so, as in {haksa sakmahmah}, find very hard; also the causing <sak> with <mahmah>
<sak> and <mawk> written as one word after a verb or describing word: a thing is made to happen or is regarded so, said with surprise or regret
people of the upper or northern part of the land, said in a pair with the word for the people of the lower or southern part, {sakmi-khangmi}
noun form of the causative <sak>: the act, place or time of making something be so, as in {lungdam sakna}, what pleases, and {kisian’ sakna mun}, a place of refining
noun form of <sa>, sing: singing, in {la sakna}, the singing of songs
noun form of <sa>, feel or regard as: the feeling so named, as in {nuam sakna}, delight, what one finds pleasant
<sakna>, singing, with plural <te>; {la saknate}, the singing of songs, and with <tum>, play, the instruments of song
in {nuam a saknate}, the things one finds pleasant, from <sa>, feel or regard as

<sak> and the ending <ni> written as one word after a describing word or verb: let us make it so, let us regard it as, as in {thupi sakni}, let us hold it important; in one sentence it is instead <sak> with <ni>, day

terms: want to make/want to let/wish to cause
definition: the causative <sak> and <nop>, want, written as one word after a verb: want to make or let that happen, as {muh saknop}, want to show
<sak>, here sing, with <nop>, want: want or like to sing
<sak>, make or cause, and <nuam>, want, written as one word after a verb: want to make something happen, or to make someone do or become something
seen once of a gate, {Benjamin Kongpi saknung}, where the English has the Upper Gate of Benjamin
<sa>, meat, with <koih>, put by: meat that was set aside; {sakoih laite} is what is left of the meat kept from the main day of <Khuado>, eaten together on the second day
the horse, in the Bible mostly an animal of war; {sakol tuangte} are horsemen and {sakol galkapte} cavalry
<sakol> written with a capital, at the start of a sentence and in the name {Sakol Kongpi}, the Horse Gate
<sakol>, horse, with the plural ending {-te} written with a hyphen; on the page the ending closes a list of words of which <Sakol> is the last
a quarter on the edge of <Tedim> town, where the high school stands
a ward of the town of Tedim in Chin State
<sakol>, horse, and <leeng>, cart: a horse-drawn chariot
<sakolleeng>, chariot, with the plural <te>
<sakol>, horse, with <leng>, cart: horse-drawn war carts; <te> marks the plural
<sakol> horse with <no>, young: a young horse
<sakol> horse with <pi>, female, and plural <te>
<sakol> horse with <tal>, the male of an animal
<sakol>, horse, with the plural <te>

causative <sak> with the male ending <pa>, placed after a verb: the one who causes it or makes it happen, he who made; also the one to whom it was done, as in {a nuntakkik sakpa}, the one who was raised
the causative <sak> and <pah>, at once, written as one word after a verb: have it done at once; {kipuak sakpah} is was sent at once
the causative <sak> with <pan>, begin, written as one word after a verb: begin to make something happen, as {paikhia sakpan}, begin to take out; in other sentences {sakpan} is from the north
<sak>, form of <sa> regard or think to be, with <pen> most; {hoih na sakpen} is what seems best to you

terms: the one that caused/the one that made
definition: the causative <sak> after a verb, with <pen>, which marks what is spoken about: the one that made something happen, as {hongngah sakpen}, what made us get it; not {sakpen}, regard as most
<sak> hard with <pen> most and the plural <te>: the hardest ones, said of rock
the causative <sak> and <phot>, for the time being, written as one word after a verb: have something done for now, temporarily; {khakcip sakphot} is have it closed for the time being
the causative <sak> and <photding> written as one word after a verb: will have it done, or let it be so, for the time being

terms: sing along with/sing together with/join in singing
definition: <sak>, the form of sing used before an ending, with <pih>, together with: sing a song along with someone

terms: feel with/share the feeling of/regard likewise
definition: <sak>, the form of feel or consider, with <pih>, together with: feel a thing as someone else feels it or regard it as they do, as {thupi sakpih}, count important with them, and {hoih sakpih}, approve
the causative <sak> with <sa>, already done, after a verb: that has been made or caused to, as in {kisiang saksa}, refined
<sak>, the form of <sa>, sing, with <sa>, already: of a song that has already been sung, as in the rules of a singing contest; here <sak> is not the causative
<sak> hard, with the causative <sak>: used of hardening the heart
the causative <sak> doubled after a verb: made someone do a thing, perhaps again and again
<sak>, sing, doubled: sing a song again and again or as a habit, with <la>, song, close by, as {tu-a i saksak la}, the song we sing today; not the causative
<sa>, sing, with the causing <sak> and the noun ending {-na}: the act or occasion of having a song sung or a piece played

terms: intend to make/try to have done
definition: <sak> and <sawm> written as one word after a verb: intend or try to make someone do the action, or to have it done
the causative <sak> and the emphatic particle <se> written as one word after a verb: just let or make it happen

terms: ought to regard as/be worth considering
definition: <sak>, form of <sa> regard or think to be, with <taak> worthy; {lamdang na saktaak} is what you ought to find astonishing
the verb ending <sak>, cause or make, or <sak> from <sa>, consider, followed by the plural <te>: those who cause, those made, those considered; {pian’ sakte} are the created things
causative <sak> and <thei>, able, written as one word after a verb: can make it happen, can cause to

terms: will be able to cause/could make
definition: <sakthei>, can cause, and <ding>, will, written as one word after a verb: it can or could make that happen

terms: can regard as/be able to consider
definition: <sak>, form of <sa>, regard or think to be, with <theih>, can, {mihoih a saktheih nading} is so that people may think them good

being able to sing; <sak>, form of <sa> sing, with <theih> can and the noun suffix <na>; {la a saktheihna ding} is so that they may sing a song

the causative <sak> and <tuam> written as one word after a verb or describing word: make it so as a further result, cause it all the more; {ziakai saktuam} is cause yet more delay
<sa>, meat, with <kuang>, bowl or trough: the dish or share of meat at a traditional feast; {sakuang hawm} is the sharing out of the meat portions

<sak> and <un> written as one word after a verb: a command to several people to do the thing for someone or to make it happen
<sak>, hard, with <zaw>, more
<sak>, cause, with <zaw>, more, placed after a verb: cause to be more so; {lungdam sakzaw} is please more
<sak> and <zawh> written as one word after a verb: be able to make that happen; the form of <sakzo> used before <nading>
form of <sa>, feel or regard as, with <zaw>, more, used before <ding> and <bangin>, {lamdang sakzawk ding} is to be held in greater awe and {na a sakzawk} is feels more pain
<sak>, cause or let, and <zel>, repeatedly, written as one word after a verb: make or let it be done time after time
<sak> and <zia> written as one word after a verb: the way in which something is made to happen or is done to someone
the causative <sak>, do to or for someone, and <ziau>, quickly and lightly, written as one word after a verb: simply do it to someone or to their thing, just like that
<sak> and <zo> written as one word after a verb: be able to make that happen, as in {kikhel sakzo}, can make something change

<sal> written with a capital, at the start of a sentence and in {Sal Suakta}, freed slaves, the name of the Freedmen
<sal>, captive, with the ending <a>: {sala om} is live as a captive, {sala mat} is take as a captive
<sa>, meat, with <laak>, take: the cuts taken out before the meat of a funeral animal is divided, of which the householders keep some and share out the rest
title placed before the name of a man among some Chin peoples; also said of a man who bears it
<sa>, flesh, with <lam>, side: the bodily or worldly side of life, set against <khalam>, the spiritual side
city on the east coast of Cyprus where Barnabas and Saul preached in the synagogues
town in Selangor, Malaysia, known for its hospital; the Malay spelling is Selayang
frankincense, a fragrant resin burned as incense; usually in {saledi paknamtui}
town on the eastern border of Bashan, in the kingdom of Og
<sa>, here think or feel a thing to be so, with <lel>, just, written as one word after a describing word: simply find it so, just suppose
city of which Melchizedek was king, taken to be Jerusalem
a man whose work is selling goods, as in {Car Salesman}
<sa>, meat, with <liang>, shoulder: the shoulder of a slaughtered animal, a share given in honour at a feast
<sa>, here feel or find, and <liang>, even, written as one word after a describing word: feel it to that degree, as {lamdang bang saliang}, find it quite strange
place near Aenon, where John was baptizing
<sal>, captive, with the suffix <in>: {salin man} is take captive, {salin paipih} is carry into exile
a Benjamite who settled in Jerusalem after the exile; also the name of a priestly family
name of two men: a Benjamite, son of Meshullam, who settled in Jerusalem after the exile, and a leader of the priests who returned with Zerubbabel
name of two men: the father of Boaz, called Salmon in Ruth, and a descendant of Caleb, founder of Bethlehem
son of Nahshon and father of Boaz, an ancestor of David
cape at the eastern end of the island of Crete
<sal> and <neih> written as one word: the keeping of slaves; {salneih ngeina} is the practice of slavery
<sa> in the sense of feel or consider, with the negative <lo>, written as one word after a describing word: not find it so, as {hoih salo}, not think it good, and {thupi salo}, not consider important
woman who followed Jesus, watched the crucifixion from a distance and came to the tomb with spices
